review.notes: Built on the course: P2P cycle, three-way match, spend analysis, Kraljic, RFI/RFQ/RFP, pre-qualification, weighted and price scoring, TCO, landed cost and Incoterms, BATNA, ZOPA, interests. Calculations checked. Fictional companies.

content.company: Highland Beverages (fictional), a juice and water bottler buying packaging, sugar and services
content.briefing: Your packaging contract ends in 8 weeks. You must run a fair tender for bottles and caps, keep daily purchasing clean, and negotiate better terms. The finance director wants savings and no supply risk.

variants.text: A supplier invoice arrives for 10,000 caps at Kz 12. The PO says Kz 11, and the goods received note shows 9,600 caps.

choices.t: Hold payment and resolve price and quantity
choices.f: Three-way match failed on both. You pay 9,600 at Kz 11 after the supplier corrects it.

choices.t: Pay the invoice; the supplier is trusted
choices.f: You overpay for 400 caps not received and a price not agreed.

choices.t: Pay the PO amount for 10,000 caps
choices.f: Price is right, but you still pay for caps never received.

variants.text: A manager orders printing work by phone and sends the invoice to you after the job is done. There is no PO.

choices.t: Escalate it: no PO means no commitment check
choices.f: The PO is the legal commitment. A retrospective PO needs approval and a lesson.

choices.t: Create a PO now so the invoice can be paid
choices.f: It pays the supplier, but hides the control failure.

choices.t: Pay it; the work was done and it is small
choices.f: Bypassing POs is how spending gets out of control.

variants.text: Bottles: high spend, big effect on cost, but only one supplier in the region can make your bottle shape. Kraljic quadrant?

choices.t: Strategic: high impact, high supply risk
choices.f: Partner and secure supply, while you work on a second source over time.

choices.t: Leverage: high impact, low risk
choices.f: Supply risk is high with one capable supplier. Competition is limited.

choices.t: Non-critical: simplify and automate
choices.f: High spend and high risk are anything but non-critical.

variants.text: Sugar: high spend, many suppliers, easy to switch. Kraljic quadrant and approach?

choices.t: Leverage: use competition to get better terms
choices.f: High impact, low risk. A competitive tender cuts the price by 6%.

choices.t: Strategic: sign a long exclusive partnership
choices.f: You give away leverage in an open market.

choices.t: Bottleneck: secure supply at any price
choices.f: Supply risk is low. Bottleneck items are low impact, high risk.

variants.text: Before writing category plans, the director asks where to start.

choices.t: Spend analysis: 12 months of spend by category
choices.f: Three categories hold 70% of spend. You focus there first.

choices.t: Call every supplier for a 10% discount
choices.f: Without data, you chase small suppliers and miss the big ones.

choices.t: Start with the newest suppliers
choices.f: New is not important. Value decides priority.

variants.text: A special label glue costs little, but only one supplier makes it and lines stop without it.

choices.t: Bottleneck: secure supply, buffer stock
choices.f: Low impact, high risk. A buffer and a second source protect the lines.

choices.t: Non-critical: buy it from the cheapest
choices.f: There is only one supplier. Risk, not price, is the issue.

choices.t: Leverage: run a tender to cut the price
choices.f: No competition exists. A tender changes nothing.

variants.text: You know exactly what bottle you need: size, weight, colour and quantity. Which request do you send?

choices.t: RFQ: a price for a clearly specified item
choices.f: Clear specs mean suppliers compete on price and terms.

choices.t: RFI: to learn what the market offers
choices.f: You already know what you need.

choices.t: RFP: proposals for a solution
choices.f: RFP suits open problems. Here the spec is fixed.

variants.text: You want to reduce plastic but do not know which packaging options exist.

choices.t: RFI first, to learn the market
choices.f: You learn about lighter bottles and recycled resin before writing specs.

choices.t: RFQ for the current bottle
choices.f: That prices what you already buy, not new options.

choices.t: Award to the current supplier
choices.f: No market check. You may miss better options.

variants.text: When do you set the evaluation criteria and weights?

choices.t: Before opening any bids
choices.f: Weights set in advance keep the tender fair and defensible.

choices.t: After reading bids, to fit the best one
choices.f: Changing weights after seeing bids is bias.

choices.t: Only if two bids are very close
choices.f: Criteria are always set first, not as a tie-breaker.

variants.text: A cheap new supplier has no tax registration proof and no references.

choices.t: Not pre-qualified: exclude until documents arrive
choices.f: Legal, financial and capacity checks come before price.

choices.t: Accept: price is what matters most
choices.f: An unregistered supplier is a legal and supply risk.

choices.t: Accept, with half payment in advance
choices.f: You add cash risk to legal risk.

variants.text: Price is worth 40 points. Lowest bid Kz 400 per 1,000 bottles. Bidder B quotes Kz 500. B's price score?

choices.t: 32 points
choices.f: Correct: 400 / 500 x 40.

choices.t: 40 points
choices.f: Only the lowest price gets full marks.

choices.t: 50 points
choices.f: You divided the wrong way. Lowest / their price x max.

variants.text: Weights: price 40%, quality 35%, delivery 25%. Bidder A scores 4, 5, 3 (out of 5). Weighted score?

choices.f: That is the simple average. Apply the weights.
That is the sum of scores without weights.

variants.text: Caps quoted FOB USD 20,000. Freight USD 3,000, insurance USD 230. What is the CIF value?

choices.f: Correct: FOB + freight + insurance. Duties and port costs come on top.
That is FOB. Under FOB you pay the freight and insurance.
Insurance is missing.

variants.text: Supplier X is 8% cheaper per bottle but rejects run at 4%, against 0.5% for supplier Y. What do you compare?

choices.t: Total cost of ownership, including rejects
choices.f: Rejects, line stops and claims cancel most of the 8%.

choices.t: Unit price only; X is cheaper
choices.f: Price is only part of the cost.

choices.t: Payment terms only
choices.f: Terms matter, but quality cost is the big gap here.

variants.text: Before negotiating with the bottle supplier, what gives you walk-away power?

choices.t: A real BATNA: a qualified second supplier
choices.f: With an alternative in hand, you can say no to a bad deal.

choices.t: A tough, fixed opening position
choices.f: Positions without alternatives are bluffs.

choices.t: The size of your company
choices.f: Size helps, but the alternative is what gives power.

variants.text: Your maximum is USD 520 per tonne. The seller's minimum is USD 480. Is there a deal zone?

choices.t: Yes: between 480 and 520
choices.f: ZOPA exists because buyer max is above seller min.

choices.t: No: you both want different prices
choices.f: Different positions are normal. The zone is what overlaps.

choices.t: Only at exactly 500
choices.f: Any price from 480 to 520 is possible.

variants.text: The supplier refuses any price cut. You learn they want steady volume to plan production.

choices.t: Offer a volume forecast for a better price
choices.f: You trade a variable they value. Price falls 3%.

choices.t: Insist on the cut or end the talks
choices.f: Positions clash and nothing moves.

choices.t: Accept the price to keep the relationship
choices.f: You give in without testing other variables.

variants.text: In the tender debrief, a losing supplier asks why they lost.

choices.t: Explain their scores against the criteria
choices.f: Fair and useful. They improve and bid stronger next time.

choices.t: Show them the winner's prices
choices.f: That breaks confidentiality.

choices.t: Say the decision is final, nothing more
choices.f: Correct but unhelpful. A debrief improves future bids.

variants.text: Received 5,000 juice cartons; 300 are damaged. What do you record?

choices.t: GRN for 4,700 and a claim for 300
choices.f: The shortage is noted at receipt, so the claim is easy.

choices.t: GRN for 5,000; damage happens
choices.f: You pay for 300 unusable cartons.

choices.t: Reject the whole delivery
choices.f: Possible, but production needs the 4,700 good cartons.

variants.text: The new packaging contract is signed. How do you manage the supplier?

choices.t: Agreed KPIs and regular performance reviews
choices.f: On-time delivery and quality are tracked and reviewed every quarter.

choices.t: Only when problems are reported
choices.f: Problems grow unnoticed between complaints.

choices.t: Retender every three months
choices.f: Constant tenders destroy the relationship and cost time.
